# fivenines_temperature_sensors (Data Source)

The sensor INVENTORY on this instance -- not the readings. The temperature itself is a metric series (`temperature`, labelled by `sensor_id` and `category`); this is what makes that series legible, turning "71.0 on coretemp-core-3" into "Core 3, critical at 100". Join the two on `sensor_id`.

NULL THRESHOLDS ARE COMMON AND MEAN "the chip declares none" -- not zero, and not "no limit". Plenty of drivers expose a reading with no high or critical point at all, and a rule that treats a null as 0 fires on every one of them.

This collector has no toggle and no version floor: every agent reports the sensors it finds, so `collector.enabled` and `collector.supported` are always true and there is no switch to look for. An empty list means this hardware exposes no sensors. `stale` is an HOUR here, not the ten minutes the per-tick collectors use, because the question is whether the sensor is still present.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The sensor inventory, not the readings -- join to the `temperature` metric
# series on sensor_id for the actual values.
data "fivenines_temperature_sensors" "cpu" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.web.id
  category    = "cpu"
}

output "cpu_sensor_labels" {
  value = {
    for s in data.fivenines_temperature_sensors.cpu.temperature_sensors :
    s.sensor_id => coalesce(s.label, s.sensor_id)
  }
}

# A null threshold means the chip declares none -- not zero, and not "no
# limit". An alert rule that treats null as 0 fires on every one of them.
output "sensors_with_a_critical_point" {
  value = {
    for s in data.fivenines_temperature_sensors.cpu.temperature_sensors :
    s.sensor_id => s.critical_threshold if s.critical_threshold != null
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `category` (String) Filter by subsystem. One of: `cpu`, `gpu`, `storage`, `network`, `chipset`, `other`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the sensor id or label.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter. The window here is an HOUR, not the ten minutes the per-tick collectors use, because the question is whether the sensor is still PRESENT. Omit for both.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `temperature_sensors` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--temperature_sensors))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--temperature_sensors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `temperature_sensors`

Read-Only:

- `category` (String) Which subsystem the sensor belongs to. One of: `cpu`, `gpu`, `storage`, `network`, `chipset`, `other`.
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `critical_threshold` (String) Degrees Celsius. Null means none is declared -- see `high_threshold`.
- `high_threshold` (String) Degrees Celsius, as the chip declares it. NULL MEANS THE CHIP DECLARES NONE -- not zero, and not "no limit". Plenty of drivers expose a reading with no threshold at all.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `label` (String) The human label the driver supplies. Null is common -- `sensor_id` is always present, this is not.
- `last_seen_at` (String) `last_seen_at`, NOT `last_synced_at` -- the column this collector carries, and what `stale` is derived from.
- `sensor_id` (String) The identity, and the label the metric series is keyed on. This is the join back to metrics/query for the actual readings.
- `sensor_type` (String) The driver or chip reporting it.
- `stale` (Boolean) The sensor has not been seen for an HOUR -- not the ten minutes every per-tick collector uses. This table is an inventory, so the question is whether the sensor is still PRESENT, and one missed tick does not remove hardware.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
